identifier_heavy.definition: The question names a rare string from the source: a model, a dataset, an option name, a number, a symbol. Lexical matching is expected to do well on these, and a retriever that keeps identifiers apart is expected to beat one that embeds the question and hopes.

paraphrase.definition: The question asks about the same content as a passage without reusing that passage's wording. No rare string carries the question to its answer, so a retriever has to match meaning rather than tokens. This is the share the claim expects dense retrieval to win.

multi_hop.definition: The question cannot be answered from one location: two or more passages have to be combined. Each question lists the locations it needs, starting with its own, because a retriever that returns one of the two has not answered it. Every extra location is a section no other question is filed under, so one retrieved passage cannot count for two questions.

unanswerable.definition: The question has no correct answer anywhere in the domain, so a system that answers it confidently is visibly wrong. Each question names nothing, and carries the string a correct answer would have to name so the corpus can be checked for support. These are what make citation accuracy mean something: without them a fabricated citation still lands on a real document.

questions.gold_answer: masking out (setting to −∞) all values in the input of the softmax

questions.gold_answer: 78.4% vs. 59.1% for top-20 accuracy on Natural Questions

questions.question: Which two kinds of wrong passage does the best configuration train against?
